chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Abu Baseer said to him, 'What do you say regarding the Prayer in the month of Ramadan?' He said, 'For the month of Ramadan is a sanctity and a right, unlike any of the other months. Pray what you are able to during the month of Ramadan, voluntarily by night and by day. So if you are able to pray a thousand cycles (rak'ah) every day and night, then do so. Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) at the end of his life used to pray a thousand cycles every day and night. So pray, O Abu Muhammad, an increase during Ramadan.'

So I said, 'How much? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'For the twenty nights, you should pray during every night twenty cycles - eight cycles being before the dusk (Isha), and twelve cycles after it, besides what you were praying before. So when the last ten days enter, pray thirty cycles during every night - eight cycles being before the dusk, and twenty-two cycles after it, besides what you were doing before that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of voluntary night prayers to perform during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific structure of increased voluntary night prayers (Qiyam) during Ramadan, prescribing twenty rak'ahs for the first twenty nights and thirty for the final ten, a practice rooted in the tradition of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). It highlights the unique sanctity of Ramadan as a month of distinct spiritual rights, encouraging believers to maximize devotion through extended night worship. This specific allocation reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on imitating the Ahl al-Bayt's rigorous devotional routines to attain spiritual elevation during the month of fasting.
